Muster

MUS-ter -- rhymes with 'cluster'. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To muster to collect, assemble, or gather, especially strength, support, or courage.

The captain ordered the entire crew to muster on deck before sunrise for inspection.

Worked Example

Standing in the wings with shaking hands, the understudy takes three slow breaths, gathers every scrap of confidence she has, and walks out onto the stage.

That deliberate gathering-up of courage before a daunting moment is exactly what it means to muster. You can muster troops, muster support, or muster your nerve -- in every case, you are pulling scattered resources together for a purpose.

How Muster Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

gather

gather: to bring together into one place

assemble

assemble: to bring together in an organized way

summon

summon: to call up or call forth, often with effort

Antonyms

disperse

disperse: to scatter in different directions

disband

disband: to break up an organized group

How Strong Is It? — gather → muster → summon

gather vs. muster

gather vs. muster: Gather is looser and more everyday than muster -- you can gather leaves or gather friends casually, while to muster implies purpose and effort, pulling things together for a challenge or a task.

summon vs. muster

summon vs. muster: Summon can carry even more effort and formality than muster: you muster courage by collecting what you have, while summoning courage suggests calling it up from somewhere deep, almost commanding it to appear.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — monstr-/mostr-

root — monstr-/mostr-: to show (Latin monstrare, via Old French mostrer)

Put it together

Put it together: Muster comes through Old French mostrer from Latin monstrare, 'to show.' Originally, to muster troops meant to assemble them for display and inspection -- gathering everyone together to show their numbers and readiness. From there it spread to gathering anything, including courage.

Use the root in a new word: demonstrate

Use the root in a new word: demonstrate: The engineer used a small model to demonstrate how the bridge would handle heavy loads.

Root Check

Word Choice

Muster shines in the pattern 'muster the courage to...' or 'muster the strength to...' -- gathering inner resources for a determined effort. It also keeps its old military sense: soldiers muster for inspection, and something that 'passes muster' is good enough to survive one.
